verses.zh: 希西家王听见，就撕裂衣服，披上麻布，进了耶和华的殿；
verses.en: When King Hezekiah heard this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went to the Lord’s temple.

verses.zh: 使家宰以利亚敬和书记舍伯那，并祭司中的长老，都披上麻布，去见亚摩斯的儿子先知以赛亚，
verses.en: He sent Eliakim the palace supervisor, Shebna the scribe, and the leading priests,[NOTE:1] clothed in sackcloth, to the prophet Isaiah son of Amoz.
notes: Heb “elders of the priests.”

verses.zh: 对他说：「希西家如此说：『今日是急难、责罚、凌辱的日子，就如妇人将要生产婴孩，却没有力量生产。
verses.en: They told him, “This is what Hezekiah says: ‘This is a day of distress, insults,[NOTE:1] and humiliation,[NOTE:2] as when a baby is ready to leave the birth canal, but the mother lacks the strength to push it through.[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “rebuke,” “correction.”
Or “contempt.”
Heb “when sons come to the cervical opening and there is no strength to give birth.”

verses.zh: 或者耶和华―你的　神听见拉伯沙基的一切话，就是他主人亚述王打发他来辱骂永生　神的话，耶和华―你的　神听见这话，就发斥责。故此，求你为余剩的民扬声祷告。』」
verses.en: Perhaps the Lord your God will hear all these things the chief adviser has spoken on behalf of his master, the king of Assyria, who sent him to taunt the living God.[NOTE:1] When the Lord your God hears, perhaps he will punish him for the things he has said.[NOTE:2] So pray for this remnant that remains.’”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “all the words of the chief adviser whom his master, the king of Assyria, sent to taunt the living God.”
Heb “and rebuke the words which the Lord your God hears.”
Heb “and lift up a prayer on behalf of the remnant that is found.”

verses.zh: 希西家王的臣仆就去见以赛亚。
verses.en: When King Hezekiah’s servants came to Isaiah,

verses.zh: 以赛亚对他们说：「要这样对你们的主人说，耶和华如此说：『你听见亚述王的仆人亵渎我的话，不要惧怕。
verses.en: Isaiah said to them, “Tell your master this: ‘This is what the Lord has said: “Don’t be afraid because of the things you have heard, because the Assyrian king’s officers have insulted me.

verses.zh: 我必惊动（原文是使灵进入）他的心，他要听见风声就归回本地。我必使他在那里倒在刀下。』」
verses.en: Look, I will take control of his mind;[NOTE:1] he will receive[NOTE:2] a report and return to his own land. I will cut him down[NOTE:3] with a sword in his own land.”’”
notes: Heb “I will put in him a spirit.” The precise sense of רוּחַ (ruakh), “spirit,” is uncertain in this context. It may refer to a spiritual being who will take control of his mind (see 1 Kgs 22:19), or it could refer to a disposition of concern and fear. In either case the Lord’s sovereignty over the king is apparent.
Heb “hear.”
Heb “cause him to fall,” that is, “kill him.”

verses.zh: 拉伯沙基回去，正遇见亚述王攻打立拿，原来他早听见亚述王拔营离开拉吉。
verses.en: When the chief adviser heard the king of Assyria had departed from Lachish, he left and went to Libnah, where the king was campaigning.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and the chief adviser returned and he found the king of Assyria fighting against Libnah, for he heard that he had departed from Lachish.”

verses.zh: 亚述王听见人论古实王特哈加说：「他出来要与你争战。」于是亚述王又打发使者去见希西家，吩咐他们说：
verses.en: The king[NOTE:1] heard that King Tirhakah of Ethiopia was marching out to fight him.[NOTE:2] He again sent messengers to Hezekiah, ordering them:
notes: Heb “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
Heb “heard concerning Tirhakah king of Cush, ‘Look, he has come out to fight with you.’”

verses.zh: 「你们对犹大王希西家如此说：『不要听你所倚靠的　神欺哄你，说耶路撒冷必不交在亚述王的手中。
verses.en: “Tell King Hezekiah of Judah this: ‘Don’t let your God in whom you trust mislead you when he says, “Jerusalem will not be handed over[NOTE:1] to the king of Assyria.”
notes: Heb “will not be given in the hand.”

verses.zh: 你总听说亚述诸王向列国所行的，乃是尽行灭绝，难道你还能得救吗？
verses.en: Certainly you have heard how the kings of Assyria have annihilated all lands.[NOTE:1] Do you really think you will be rescued?[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Look, you have heard what the kings of Assyria have done to all the lands, annihilating them.”
Heb “and will you be rescued?” The rhetorical question expects the answer, “No, of course not!”

verses.zh: 我列祖所毁灭的，就是歌散、哈兰、利色，和属提．拉撒的伊甸人，这些国的神何曾拯救这些国呢？
verses.en: Were the nations whom my ancestors destroyed—the nations of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, and the people of Eden in Telassar—rescued by their gods?[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Did the gods of the nations whom my fathers destroyed rescue them—Gozan and Haran, and Rezeph and the sons of Eden who are in Telassar?”

verses.zh: 哈马的王、亚珥拔的王、西法瓦音城的王、希拿，和以瓦的王都在哪里呢？』」
verses.en: Where are the king of Hamath, the king of Arpad, and the kings of Lair,[NOTE:1] Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivvah?’”
notes: Lair is a city located in northeastern Babylon. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 235.

verses.zh: 希西家从使者手里接过书信来，看完了，就上耶和华的殿，将书信在耶和华面前展开。
verses.en: Hezekiah took the letter[NOTE:1] from the messengers and read it.[NOTE:2] Then Hezekiah went up to the Lord’s temple and spread it out before the Lord.
notes: The MT has the plural, “letters,” but the final mem is probably dittographic (note the initial mem on the form that immediately follows). Some Greek and Aramaic witnesses have the singular.

The MT has the plural suffix, “them,” but this probably reflects a later harmonization to the preceding textual issue concerning the plural word “letters.” The parallel passage in Isa 37:14 has the singular suffix.

verses.zh: 希西家向耶和华祷告说：「坐在二基路伯上耶和华―以色列的　神啊，你是天下万国的　神，你曾创造天地。
verses.en: Hezekiah prayed before the Lord: “Lord God of Israel, who is enthroned above the cherubim![NOTE:1] You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made the sky[NOTE:2] and the earth.
notes: This refers to the cherub images that were above the ark of the covenant.
Or “the heavens.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，求你侧耳而听！耶和华啊，求你睁眼而看！要听西拿基立打发使者来辱骂永生　神的话。
verses.en: Pay attention, Lord, and hear! Open your eyes, Lord, and observe! Listen to the message Sennacherib sent and how he taunts the living God![NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “Hear the words of Sennacherib which he sent to taunt the living God.”

verses.zh: 耶和华啊，亚述诸王果然使列国和列国之地变为荒凉，
verses.en: It is true, Lord, that the kings of Assyria have destroyed the nations and their lands.

verses.zh: 将列国的神像都扔在火里；因为它本不是神，乃是人手所造的，是木头石头的，所以灭绝它。
verses.en: They have burned the gods of the nations,[NOTE:1] for they are not really gods, but only the product of human hands manufactured from wood and stone. That is why the Assyrians could destroy them.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “and they put their gods in the fire.”
Heb “so they destroyed them.”

verses.zh: 耶和华―我们的　神啊，现在求你救我们脱离亚述王的手，使天下万国都知道惟独你―耶和华是　神！」
verses.en: Now, O Lord our God, rescue us from his power, so that all the kingdoms of the earth will know that you, Lord, are the only God.”

verses.zh: 亚摩斯的儿子以赛亚就打发人去见希西家，说：「耶和华―以色列的　神如此说：『你既然求我攻击亚述王西拿基立，我已听见了。』
verses.en: Isaiah son of Amoz sent this message to Hezekiah: “This is what the Lord God of Israel has said: ‘I have heard your prayer[NOTE:1] concerning King Sennacherib of Assyria.
notes: Heb “what you have prayed to me.”

verses.zh: 耶和华论他这样说：锡安的处女藐视你，嗤笑你；耶路撒冷的女子向你摇头。
verses.en: This is what the Lord says about him:[NOTE:1] “‘“The virgin daughter Zion[NOTE:2] despises you, she makes fun of you;Daughter Jerusalem shakes her head after you.[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “this is the word which the Lord has spoken about him.”

Zion (Jerusalem) is pictured here as a young, vulnerable daughter whose purity is being threatened by the would-be Assyrian rapist. The personification hints at the reality which the young girls of the city would face if the Assyrians conquer it.
Shaking the head was a mocking gesture of derision.

verses.zh: 你辱骂谁？亵渎谁？扬起声来，高举眼目攻击谁呢？乃是攻击以色列的圣者！
verses.en: Whom have you taunted and hurled insults at?At whom have you shouted,[NOTE:1] and looked so arrogantly?[NOTE:2] At the Holy One of Israel![NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “have you raised a voice.”
Heb “and lifted your eyes on high?”
This divine title pictures the Lord as the sovereign king who rules over his covenant people and exercises moral authority over them.

verses.zh: 你藉你的使者辱骂主，并说：我率领许多战车上山顶，到黎巴嫩极深之处；我要砍伐其中高大的香柏树和佳美的松树；我必上极高之处，进入肥田的树林。
verses.en: Through your messengers you taunted the Sovereign Master,[NOTE:1] ‘With my many chariots[NOTE:2] I climbed up the high mountains, the slopes of Lebanon.I cut down its tall cedarsand its best evergreens.I invaded its most remote regions,[NOTE:3] its thickest woods.
notes: The word is אֲדֹנָי (ʾadonay), “lord,” but some Hebrew mss have יְהוָה (yehvah), “Lord.”

The consonantal text (Kethib) has בְּרֶכֶב (berekhev), but this must be dittographic (note the following רִכְבִּי [rikhbi], “my chariots”). The marginal reading (Qere) בְּרֹב (berov), “with many,” is supported by many Hebrew mss and ancient versions, as well as the parallel passage in Isa 37:24.
Heb “the lodging place of its extremity.”

verses.zh: 我已经在外邦挖井喝水；我必用脚掌踏干埃及的一切河。
verses.en: I dug wells and drankwater in foreign lands.[NOTE:1] With the soles of my feet I dried upall the rivers of Egypt.’
notes: Heb “I dug and drank foreign waters.”

verses.zh: 耶和华说，我早先所做的，古时所立的，就是现在藉你使坚固城荒废，变为乱堆，这事你岂没有听见吗？
verses.en: [NOTE:1] Certainly you must have heard![NOTE:2] Long ago I worked it out.In ancient times I planned[NOTE:3] it;and now I am bringing it to pass.The plan is this:Fortified cities will crashinto heaps of ruins.[NOTE:4]
notes: Having quoted the Assyrian king’s arrogant words in vv. 23-24, the Lord now speaks to the king.
Heb “Have you not heard?” The rhetorical question expresses the Lord’s amazement that anyone might be ignorant of what he is about to say.
Heb “formed.”

Heb “and it is to cause to crash into heaps of ruins fortified cities.” The subject of the third feminine singular verb תְּהִי (tehi) is the implied plan, referred to in the preceding lines with third feminine singular pronominal suffixes.

verses.zh: 所以其中的居民力量甚小，惊惶羞愧。他们像野草，像青菜，如房顶上的草，又如未长成而枯干的禾稼。
verses.en: Their residents are powerless,[NOTE:1] they are terrified and ashamed.They are as short-lived as plants in the field,or green vegetation.[NOTE:2] They are as short-lived as grass on the rooftops[NOTE:3] when it is scorched by the east wind.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “short of hand.”
Heb “they are plants in the field and green vegetation.” The metaphor emphasizes how short-lived these seemingly powerful cities really were. See Ps 90:5-6; Isa 40:6-8, 24.
Heb “[they are] grass on the rooftops.” See the preceding note.

The Hebrew text has “scorched before the standing grain” (perhaps meaning “before it reaches maturity”), but it is preferable to emend קָמָה (qamah), “standing grain,” to קָדִים (qadim), “east wind” (with the support of 1Q Isaa in Isa 37:27).

verses.zh: 你坐下，你出去，你进来，你向我发烈怒，我都知道。
verses.en: I know where you liveand everything you do.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “your going out and your coming in.” The MT also has here, “and how you have raged against me.” However, this line is probably dittographic (note the beginning of the next line).

verses.zh: 因你向我发烈怒，又因你狂傲的话达到我耳中，我就要用钩子钩上你的鼻子，把嚼环放在你口里，使你从你来的路转回去。
verses.en: Because you rage against me,and the uproar you create has reached my ears,[NOTE:1] I will put my hook in your nose,[NOTE:2] and my bridle between your lips,and I will lead you back the wayyou came.”
notes: Heb “and your complacency comes up into my ears.” The parallelism is improved if שַׁאֲנַנְךָ (shaʾananekha), “your complacency,” is emended to שַׁאֲוַנְךְ (shaʾavanekha), “your uproar.” See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 237-38.
The word picture has a parallel in Assyrian sculpture. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 238.

verses.zh: 「以色列人哪，我赐你们一个证据：你们今年要吃自生的，明年也要吃自长的；至于后年，你们要耕种收割，栽植葡萄园，吃其中的果子。
verses.en: [NOTE:1] “‘This will be your confirmation that I have spoken the truth:[NOTE:2] This year you will eat what grows wild,[NOTE:3] and next year[NOTE:4] what grows on its own from that. But in the third year you will plant seed and harvest crops; you will plant vines and consume their produce.[NOTE:5]
notes: At this point the word concerning the king of Assyria (vv. 21-28) ends and the Lord again directly addresses Hezekiah and the people (see v. 20).

Heb “and this is your sign.” In this case the אוֹת (ʾot), “sign,” is a future confirmation of God’s intervention designated before the actual intervention takes place. For similar “signs” see Exod 3:12 and Isa 7:14-25.
This refers to crops that grew up on their own (that is, without cultivation) from the seed planted in past years.
Heb “and in the second year.”

The four plural imperatival verb forms in v. 29b are used rhetorically. The Lord commands the people to plant, harvest, etc. to emphasize the certainty of restored peace and prosperity. See IBHS 572 §34.4.c.

verses.zh: 犹大家所逃脱余剩的，仍要往下扎根，向上结果。
verses.en: Those who remain in Judah will take root in the ground and bear fruit.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “The remnant of the house of Judah that is left will add roots below and produce fruit above.”

verses.zh: 必有余剩的民从耶路撒冷而出；必有逃脱的人从锡安山而来。耶和华的热心必成就这事。
verses.en: “‘For a remnant will leave Jerusalem; survivors will come out of Mount Zion.The zeal of the Lord of Heaven’s Armies[NOTE:1] will accomplish this.
notes: Traditionally “the Lord of hosts.” In this context the Lord’s “zeal” refers to his intense devotion to and love for his people which prompts him to protect and restore them. The Qere, along with many medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions, has “the zeal of the Lord of hosts” rather than “the zeal of the Lord” (Kethib). The translation follows the Qere here.

verses.zh: 「所以，耶和华论亚述王如此说：『他必不得来到这城，也不在这里射箭，不得拿盾牌到城前，也不筑垒攻城。
verses.en: So this is what the Lord has said about the king of Assyria: “He will not enter this city,nor will he shoot an arrow here.[NOTE:1] He will not attack it with his shield-carrying warriors,[NOTE:2] nor will he build siege works against it.
notes: Heb “there.”
Heb “[with] a shield.” By metonymy the “shield” stands for the soldier who carries it.

verses.zh: 他从哪条路来，必从那条路回去，必不得来到这城。这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: He will go back the way he came.He will not enter this city,” says the Lord.

verses.zh: 因我为自己的缘故，又为我仆人大卫的缘故，必保护拯救这城。』」
verses.en: “‘I will shield this city and rescue it for the sake of my reputation and because of my promise to David my servant.’”[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “for my sake and for the sake of David my servant.”

verses.zh: 当夜，耶和华的使者出去，在亚述营中杀了十八万五千人。清早有人起来，一看，都是死尸了。
verses.en: That very night the angel of the Lord went out and killed 185,000 in the Assyrian camp. When they[NOTE:1] got up early the next morning, there were all the corpses.[NOTE:2]
notes: This refers to the Israelites and/or the rest of the Assyrian army.
Heb “look, all of them were dead bodies.”

verses.zh: 亚述王西拿基立就拔营回去，住在尼尼微。
verses.en: So King Sennacherib of Assyria broke camp and went on his way. He went home and stayed in Nineveh.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “and Sennacherib king of Assyria departed and went and returned and lived in Nineveh.”

verses.zh: 一日在他的神尼斯洛庙里叩拜，他儿子亚得米勒和沙利色用刀杀了他，就逃到亚拉腊地。他儿子以撒哈顿接续他作王。
verses.en: One day,[NOTE:1] as he was worshiping in the temple of his god Nisroch,[NOTE:2] his sons[NOTE:3] Adrammelech and Sharezer struck him down with the sword.[NOTE:4] They escaped to the land of Ararat; his son Esarhaddon replaced him as king.
notes: The assassination probably took place in 681 b.c.

No such Mesopotamian god is presently known. Perhaps the name Nisroch is a textual variation of Nusku, the Mesopotamian god of light and fire. Other proposals have tried to relate the name to Ashur, the chief god of the Assyria, or to Ninurta, the Assyrian god of war.
Although “his sons” is absent in the Kethib, it is supported by the Qere, along with many medieval Hebrew mss and the ancient versions. Cf. Isa 37:38.
Extra-biblical sources also mention the assassination of Sennacherib, though they refer to only one assassin. See M. Cogan and H. Tadmor, II Kings (AB), 239-40.
